messages:
mei: seeing a p99 spike starting ~1850123450 across us-west hosts. SLO alert fired. Not a CPU shortage, but tail latency jumped 3-4x. Any recent runtime changes?
devin: we merged a kernel selector tweak at 1850123440 (rollout to canary then prod). Could be related.
sanjay: also noticed kv-cache eviction rate shot up at the same time on a subset of nodes. Noisy tenant maybe. eviction_rate p95 0.2 -> 0.9.
alex: dashboards disagree: ops dashboard shows high request latency but traces page only has ~10% of expected spans (trace sampling low). That means root cause timeline messy.
mei: exact timeline: deploy 1850123440, latency rise 1850123450, eviction spike 1850123460, traces drop 1850123465. Looks correlated but need proof.
devin: quick profiler dump from one affected host: 
```
kernel_select_ms: 8 -> 46
batch_wait_ms_median: 1.1 -> 9.8
kv_cache.miss_rate: 0.18 -> 0.77
net_tx_retries: unchanged
```
mei: kernel_select jumping is suspicious — selector falling back to slower kernel path. Could be a fingerprint mismatch with quantized kernels.
sanjay: noisy neighbor hypothesis: a tenant started heavy long-context inference and caused KV pages to be evicted, increasing cold-start cost per request and triggering slower kernel path due to seqlen distribution change.
alex: compounding issue: log-sampler config was inverted in the logging rollout at ~1850123455 so sampling rate dropped for runtime spans. We missed high-fidelity traces during the initial minutes. :facepalm:
ops-bot: deploy service/runtime-selector v2.9.1 -> canary @1850123440 by dev-deploy (meta: rollout=50%, notes="selector heuristic tweak")
mei: can we roll back selector or force old kernel for affected hosts? Need immediate mitigation while we investigate KV pattern.
devin: I can force selector.allow_legacy=true for the impacted pool. Pushing change now.
ops-bot: config update pushed to pool-prod-west-1 at 1850123488 by devin.
mei: after forcing legacy selector, p99 back to normal on those hosts within ~40s. eviction_rate remained high but latency recovered.
sanjay: that suggests two factors: eviction-induced cold-cache + kernel mis-selection amplifies tail. If selector had chosen legacy fast-path for cold KV misses we wouldn't have regressed.
alex: next steps: 1) add a histogram to kernel_selector to surface confidence scores, 2) increase log sampling briefly on runtime during incidents, 3) add KV prefetch metrics to per-host dashboard (prefetch_hit, prefetch_latency), 4) investigate tenant that caused eviction.
mei: agree. Also add alert for kernel_selector.fallback_rate > 0.05 paired with kv_cache.miss_rate increase (prevent future noisy-neighbor + selector interactions).
devin: I'll make a small PR for selector confidence metrics + temporary flag to prefer legacy when kv_cache.miss_rate > 0.5.
sanjay: I'll triage eviction logs and correlate tenant ids with burst. Pls give me retention keys to pull full cache traces for the window.
alex: I'll patch dashboards to show prefetch metrics and make traces sampling override for oncall role (so we always capture full traces when SLO breaches).
mei: thanks team. Documenting timeline in incident tracker and marking as mitigated (latency restored after selector flag). Will follow up for root cause RCA once eviction owner identified. :thumbsup:
__notes: Single-thread Slack conversation covering kernel selector regression, KV cache eviction, and observability gaps (trace sampling + dashboard mismatch).
